population.erp_2025.note: ABS Estimated Resident Population, LGA 48050, 30 June 2025; 2021 mesh-block counts (S-C30) are scaled to it.

population.persons_per_household.note: Census 2021 average household size; occupied households per zone = persons / this (capped by dwellings).

population.cars_per_household.note: Census 2021; reported per zone and used for vehicle-km per car in validation (trip rates already imply car use).

population.occupied_share_new_dwellings.note: Share of new dwellings occupied by residents (76.2% in 2021); the rest are holiday homes. UGMS uses the same to turn dwellings into people.

rates.low_density.note: TfNSW Guide to Transport Impact Assessment Tables 5.3/5.4, low density residential, regional sites (2022 surveys). Excludes trips internal to a subdivision.

rates.seniors.note: TfNSW Tables 5.16/5.17, housing for seniors, regional sites (2009 surveys, 10am-8pm).

rates.senior_weight.note: Calibrated against DIT daily volumes (S-D01/S-D02) on internal arterials; default 0.42 = share aged 65+ (S-C01) under-loaded Hindmarsh Rd/Torrens St.

rates.day_type.note: Which TfNSW column each condition uses; Saturday takes the weekend rate.

rates.condition_factor.note: Extra multiplier on resident trip rates by condition (1.0 = rate as published).

rates.external_share.note: Resident trips with one end outside the study area (Port Elliot, Goolwa, Adelaide); emitted as stratum ext with the home zone as origin.

rates.external_gateway_split.note: Gateway used by residents' external trips: Adelaide via Victor Harbor Rd, Mount Compass / Strathalbyn via Hindmarsh Tiers Rd, Port Elliot/Goolwa via Port Elliot Rd.

rates.rural_inbound_share.note: Share of trips by residents of zones outside the study area that come into it (the rest stay rural or go elsewhere).

rates.nhb_share.note: Non-home-based (destination to destination) trips; origin is drawn by gravity from home, destination by gravity from that origin.

purpose.shares.note: Resident purpose mix. Work 0.16 on a term weekday = 3,379 car-driver commuters x 2 trips (S-C01) / ~42,000 resident trips; the rest reflects a retiree-heavy town (no travel survey for Victor Harbor). School = escort trips.

time.target_profile.note: Hourly profile the resident tours are fitted to: 'observed' = sim/data/profiles/hourly_profile.csv from S3 (07-18 from the 2017 counts, night hours assumed there); 'placeholder' = time.placeholder_profile.

time.placeholder_profile.note: PLACEHOLDER used only when the S3 profile is missing: midday peak per the 2017 finding that town-centre peaks are 11:15-14:15 (S-D19).

time.purpose_profiles.note: Shape priors for the outbound leg of each purpose. Resident priors are then fitted (time.fit_iterations) so that all resident trips together follow the target profile; visitor/lodging profiles are used as given.

time.fit_iterations.note: Iterations of the multiplicative fit of resident outbound profiles to the target profile (0 = no fit).

time.dwell_minutes.note: Time spent at the destination before the return trip. Trucks: a delivery stop (not a working day).

time.speed_kmh.note: Average speed used only to estimate when a return leg starts (network-distance / speed).

time.max_depart_s.note: Latest departure written (26 h) so NYE departures after midnight survive; S4 runs need end >= this.

gravity.beta.note: Halved distance decay: longer trips needed to reproduce counted cross-town flows.

gravity.detour_factor.note: Typical urban circuity; only scales distance (and so the return-leg timing and validation km).

gravity.min_distance_km.note: Floor on distance in the gravity term so a POI next door does not take all trips.

gravity.same_point_km.note: Destinations closer than this to the origin are excluded (no zero-length trips).

poi.category_map.note: Mapping of the S-E03 heuristic labels to the DESIGN categories. Parking, transport and fire stations are dropped; private swimming pools tagged as gyms are dropped (A: pools are private houses, not gyms).

poi.category_override.note: Shopping malls are tagged as food retail in S-E03; Woolworths inside Victor Central is its own POI, so the malls count as shops (avoids double-counting the supermarket pull).

poi.drop_private_pools.note: Drop leisure=swimming_pool features (30 of the 35 'gym_fitness' POIs are pools, mostly access=private).

poi.default_weight.note: Weight for a POI with no named weight. Small supermarket-category outlets (bakeries, convenience) get 0.3 against ~1-4 for full supermarkets.

poi.named_weight.unit: relative attraction (supermarkets ~ thousands of m2 floor area; parks/accommodation: sites or rooms)
poi.named_weight.note: Supermarket weights are floor-area proxies (full-line Woolworths and Coles ~3,500-3,800 m2, Drakes ~1,800, Aldi ~1,700, IGA ~800) - not measured; caravan sites and rooms are rough capacities, not from operators.

value.name: Granite Island causeway
value.source: assumption (foreshore end of the causeway, S-E01)

value.name: Encounter Bay foreshore
value.source: S-E01 way 439835772 (park on the Esplanade, Encounter Bay)

poi.extra.note: Named places from the OSM extract missing from S-E03 (parks/reserves); coordinates are way centroids.

poi.mb_categories.note: ABS mesh blocks of these categories become extra POIs (OSM has only 2 schools); weight = poi.default_weight of the category.

poi.mb_dedupe_km.note: A mesh-block POI within this distance of an OSM POI of the same category is dropped as a duplicate.

work.jobs_per_ha.unit: jobs per hectare of mesh block
work.jobs_per_ha.note: Work destinations = non-residential mesh blocks (S-C30 categories) weighted by area x job density; Commercial covers the town centre and McCracken.

work.town_centre_weight.note: Extra work weight at Victor Central (retail and service jobs in the centre on top of its mesh blocks).

work.town_centre_location.note: Victor Central Shopping Centre (S-E03 way 491901394) as the location of the town-centre work weight.

work.jobs_per_new_dwelling.note: Work weight added at the employment growth areas (Waterport Rd) in growth years.

gateways.aadt_assumed.note: Council roads without a DIT count. gw_grn (Greenhills Rd) and gw_wel (Welch Rd) are used only with the S-E01 fallback extract; with S-S1-01 both roads lie inside the network.

gateways.split.unit: fraction of the gateway's non-resident volume
gateways.split.note: Of AADT minus the residents' own crossings: through traffic (both ends outside, mostly Port Elliot/Goolwa <-> Adelaide via the McCracken roundabout), external with a local end (workers, shoppers, trades from outside), and visitors (base, non-summer day-trippers).

gateways.day_factor.note: Weekday term volumes taken as AADT; Saturday through/commuter traffic lower.

gateways.truck_cv_factor.note: Trucks per gateway = CV% x AADT x this, drawn from thr and ext vehicles. DIT CV includes light rigid trucks/buses (class 3-5).

gateways.growth_per_year.unit: fraction per year after the base year
gateways.growth_per_year.note: Growth of non-resident gateway traffic (through, external, day-trippers) in future years. 0 = held at base-year volumes; residents of new dwellings add their own trips. Hindmarsh Rd grew ~2.2%/yr 2009-2024 (S-D02), but that includes local growth; set e.g. 0.01 for a sensitivity run.

caravans.share_of_vis.note: Day-tripper and holiday-home arrivals towing a caravan/camper.

caravans.share_of_park_arrivals.note: Arrivals/departures of caravan-park parties that tow a caravan or drive a motorhome (the rest use cabins). Local trips from the park are cars.

visitors.holiday_home_occupancy.unit: fraction of unoccupied dwellings in use
visitors.holiday_home_occupancy.note: S-C14: 'over the summer holiday season most of the dwellings are occupied'.

visitors.trips_per_party.note: Local trips by staying visitors (2 tours a day).

visitors.turnover_per_day.unit: arrivals (and departures) per party per day
visitors.turnover_per_day.note: ~1/7: a one-week average stay. Each arrival and departure crosses a gateway.

visitors.arrival_gateway_split.note: Where staying visitors come from (Adelaide via Victor Harbor Rd).

visitors.purpose_shares.note: Visitor destinations: foreshore, dining and the centre.

visitors.summer_vhr_target.note: DIT: more than 11,000 vehicles/day on Victor Harbor Rd near Hindmarsh Tiers Rd / Virgin Rd and Brookman Rd in the summer peak (S-D18). With S-S1-01 gw_vhr sits on that stretch (DIT 28.26-43.21, AADT 7,700), so the target applies there directly. Day-tripper volume in summer_peak is scaled until gw_vhr reaches it.

visitors.summer_scale_all_gateways.note: Apply the Victor Harbor Rd summer day-tripper factor to the other gateways' visitor volume too.

visitors.vis_day_factor.unit: multiplier on base visitor gateway volume
visitors.vis_day_factor.note: More day-trippers on Saturdays; summer handled by the target above.

visitors.second_stop_share.note: Day-trippers that visit a second destination before leaving.

ext.purpose_shares.note: Destinations of non-residents coming in through a gateway (car trips); trucks go to work (commercial/industrial) destinations.

event.venue.note: New Year's Eve celebration venue (council events calendar).

event.attendees.note: Council Event Calendar 2026/27 expected attendance (PAX) for New Year's Eve Celebrations at Warland Reserve (was an assumption of 5,000).

event.car_share.unit: fraction of attendees arriving by car
event.car_share.note: Others walk from nearby homes and holiday parks.

event.origin_split.note: Residents, staying visitors (holiday homes, parks) and people driving in from Port Elliot/Goolwa/Adelaide.

event.arrival_window_h.note: Arrivals spread uniformly, evening build-up before the 9pm family fireworks and midnight.

event.early_departure_window_h.note: Departure window of early leavers (after the 9pm family fireworks).

event.min_stay_s.note: Minimum time at the event for early leavers who arrive late.

growth.rates.note: UGMS 2050 scenarios: moderate (historic trend) 185/yr; high = GARP targets by decade.

growth.base_year.note: Dwellings are added from the 2025 base (ERP 2025 already contains 2021-25 building, ~159/yr per S-B10 p.20).

growth.capacity.note: S-B10 p.31: zoned infill up to 4,100; Deferred Urban Zone up to 2,400 (= growth area 1); Future Greenfield ~3,600 split between areas 2 (255 ha drawn) and 3 (197 ha) by drawn area; GARP-only parcels: null = area x growth.garp_only_density_per_ha.

growth.order.note: Greenfield areas fill in council priority order (map numbering), then the GARP-only parcels.

growth.infill_share.note: Infill share while infill capacity lasts (2011-21 was 85% infill, S-C14 s.4.5, but greenfield opens up).

growth.infill_weighting.note: Infill is spread over residential mesh blocks inside the study area in proportion to their existing dwellings.

growth.cell_deg.note: Growth areas are cut into grid cells (~360 x 440 m) that become zones; dwellings split by cell area.

vtypes.note: Car: SUMO passenger defaults. Truck: rigid truck (DIT CV are mostly class 3-5). Caravan: car plus ~6 m van, slower acceleration, capped at 100 km/h; vClass passenger so caravans may use any car road.

validation.trip_length_km.unit: km (network: straight line x detour), plausible mean range
validation.trip_length_km.note: No archived trip-length norm for a town of this size: ranges reflect the urban area (~8 km from Encounter Bay to McCracken, ~4 km deep) with shops concentrated in the centre and McCracken. Replace with a travel-survey figure if one is archived.

validation.town_centre_cordon.note: Box around the town-centre streets served from Torrens St (Victoria St to Bridge Tce, Torrens St to the foreshore) used to compare with the 2017 'vehicles entering the town centre' figure.

validation.town_centre_entries_12h.note: Tonkin 2017 Torrens Street review: almost 7,600 vehicles entered the town centre in 12 h (Wed 26 Apr 2017, school holidays). Compared with trips whose destination is inside the cordon and origin outside it.

validation.vkt_reference_km_per_car_day.unit: km per passenger vehicle per day
validation.vkt_reference_km_per_car_day.note: Order of magnitude of Australian average passenger-vehicle use (~11,000 km/yr, ABS Survey of Motor Vehicle Use; not archived here). In-area driving should be well below it because trips outside the study area are cut at the gateways.

validation.max_share_to_weight_ratio.note: A supermarket is flagged when its share of supermarket trips differs from its weight share by more than this factor either way (gravity legitimately favours central stores).
